rules.title: A compiled unit is one immutable file whose address is its content and its environment
rules.divergesFromPhp: opcache's file cache is keyed by path and revalidated by timestamp; an artifact here is keyed by the source's digest and the environment's, so a file built for another machine, compiler or extension set is never opened at all

rules.title: An artifact is a self-describing header over one relocatable object, and it carries no class metadata
A compiled-unit cache entry is read into memory, never mapped
A warm hit skips codegen and nothing else, and it must beat the compile it replaces
An artifact is hashed in full where it lies, then placed, relocated and only then made executable
The checksum answers corruption; a cache directory another account can write is refused at startup
rules.divergesFromPhp: opcache.file_cache_dir is taken as written; a directory that is world-writable or not owned by the runtime's own account refuses the process rather than the entry

rules.title: A bad cache entry is a miss the script never sees, and only a corrupt one is deleted
A writer publishes by one atomic rename, and a path that already exists wins
Eviction rides the cold miss at a configured probability, and a warm hit pays nothing for it
`nvs cache gc` and `nvs cache clear` are the operator's deterministic alternative to the roll
A unit's cache key covers every autoload path it probed, misses included, and every directory a discovery query listed
rules.divergesFromPhp: OPcache revalidates the files it compiled; here adding a file that shadows an already-resolved name, or a module nothing references yet, invalidates the unit although no hashed file changed

rules.title: A compiled extension module is cached in the same store, under the same key, header and verify shape
`nvs build --compile` appends a program to a copy of the `nvs` binary, and rebundling is running it again
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `.phar` and no archive format: the shipped file is the runtime itself with the source appended, and it is remade by its author rather than updated in place

rules.title: A bundle's payload is source, as a flat file list with no archive and no compression
rules.divergesFromPhp: a `.phar` can be stripped or compressed; a bundle's source is embedded byte for byte and is recoverable by anyone who looks

rules.title: Inside a closed-world target every `require` resolves at build time, and one that cannot fails the build
rules.divergesFromPhp: an `include` whose path is computed at run time has no filesystem to fall back on inside a bundle, so the build refuses it instead of the run failing on the user's machine

rules.title: A bundle is recognised by a footer the host reads before it parses one argument
`nvs build --compile` packages what is already resolved on disk and fetches no dependency
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `composer install` step inside the bundler: resolving dependencies and packaging them are two commands that compose, not one

rules.title: A `.nvsx` the program depends on is embedded as one opaque entry of the same flat list
A macOS bundle is ad-hoc signed by the build command; PE and ELF need no step
A build records its target, host, profile, compiler, commit and the commit's own date, and never a build date
`nvs --help` opens with the README's own title and the version, commit and commit date of the build answering
`nvs.exe` carries the logo as its icon and the manifest's facts as its version information, and a debug build carries its own icon
The third-party notice is generated from the dependency graph, fails closed, and is never written by hand
The notice and Novis's own license are compiled into the binary from the same tree
No flag on `nvs` is inherited from PHP; `-h` and `-V` are the Unix baseline and `-o` the only short flag Novis declares
rules.divergesFromPhp: `php` carries `-i`, `-a`, `-r`, `-f` and a lowercase `-v`; `nvs` inherits none of them, spells every operation as a subcommand, and declares exactly one short flag of its own

rules.title: A doc comment clap renders is written for the person reading `--help`, and cites nothing they cannot open
rules.divergesFromPhp: `php --help` lists flags the manual explains elsewhere; `nvs --help` is the explanation, and it names no repository document, no decision record and no file extension the binary does not act on

rules.title: `nvs info` is the one call for build, host and licensing facts, and the one spelling of it
rules.divergesFromPhp: `php -i` prints ini settings and the request's own server variables; `nvs info` reports the build, the host and the licences, never per-request state, and it is spelled one way

rules.title: A package name is `vendor/name`, lowercase ASCII compared exactly, and `nvs` is reserved for first-party packages
rules.divergesFromPhp: Composer lowercases and compares names case-insensitively; here a name is compared exactly so that one which resolves on one operating system resolves on all three

rules.title: A package is an immutable source archive whose identity is its BLAKE3 digest
rules.divergesFromPhp: a Composer dependency is a name that resolves to whatever the registry serves today; here two archives with the same digest are the same package and two with different digests are different packages whatever they call themselves

rules.title: `package.toml` is read by the `nvs` CLI, never by the runtime and never by name resolution
rules.divergesFromPhp: composer.json drives the autoloader; here a populated `vendor/` resolves every name identically whether the manifest is present, absent or malformed

rules.title: Every file in a fetched package declares a namespace under the prefix its manifest claims, and two packages claiming one prefix is a fetch error naming both
rules.divergesFromPhp: a Composer package may declare any PSR-4 prefix, including the application's; here a package file declaring `namespace App;` to reach the application's grants fails to compile

rules.title: A fetched package is reached by an ordinary `autoload` line in a committed, generated `vendor/packages.nvs`
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `vendor/autoload.php` classmap or loader to `require`; the generated file holds declarations the compiler resolves like any other source

rules.title: Nothing in a package runs before your program does
rules.divergesFromPhp: Composer's `scripts` (`post-install-cmd` and friends) and plugins execute at install time; here there is no hook, build step, macro or code generation of any kind

rules.title: A package ships no `nvs.toml`, and none of its `require` or `autoload` paths reaches outside its own directory
rules.divergesFromPhp: a Composer package's files may `require` anything the process can read; here a `..`, an absolute path or a symlink that leaves the package is a compile error

rules.title: Resolution selects the highest minimum any package asked for, and nothing upgrades itself
rules.divergesFromPhp: there are no version ranges and no solver, so `^1.4` and "your requirements could not be resolved" both cease to exist; a version arrives only because somebody named it

rules.title: `package.lock` records every package's digest, a mismatch is a hard error, and `--locked` fetches nothing the lock does not name
rules.divergesFromPhp: composer.lock pins a version and a `dist` URL; here the lock pins bytes, and a vendored tree is re-checked against it on every build rather than trusted once

rules.title: A git dependency pins an exact commit, and only the root application may declare one
rules.divergesFromPhp: a `vcs` repository in composer.json may name a branch and is honoured anywhere in the graph; here a git source names a commit and is refused below the root, at publish and at fetch

rules.title: The registry publishes an append-only transparency log, and a client verifies inclusion and consistency before using an artifact
rules.divergesFromPhp: Packagist can serve one client different bytes than another with nothing to show for it; here a registry that does so must fork a signed log, which the next consistency check reports

rules.title: `nvs publish` uploads a clean-checkout archive, and the registry never overwrites a published `name@version`
rules.divergesFromPhp: a Packagist release is whatever tag the repository points at and can be moved; here a published version is immutable and is in the transparency log before it is downloadable

rules.title: A known-bad version is retracted, never deleted, and `nvs audit` names the minimum bump that clears it
rules.divergesFromPhp: Packagist lets a publisher delete a release, which breaks every lockfile naming it; here the bytes stay fetchable forever and only selection refuses them

rules.title: A package that breaks its API publishes under a new name carrying `supersedes`
rules.divergesFromPhp: `2.0.0` of the same name is how Composer ships a break; here the break is `acme/http2`, and the old and new package coexist in one graph without conflict

rules.title: Until 0.1.0 ships any dependency updates at any time, and the version contract starts with the commit that tags 0.1.0
A version number describes the enumerated surface, and the Rust crate APIs, the artifact cache, diagnostic prose and MSRV carry no promise
One `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` for the whole workspace, and below 1.0 the breaking slot moves left
rules.divergesFromPhp: PHP numbers a runtime that programs then target; here `nvs --version` is the language version, and `0.MINOR` rather than `MAJOR` is what carries a break until 1.0

rules.title: A change a dependency forced ships as a patch, a minor or a major by who can see it, never by how big the diff was
A dependency break that a program author could see goes down a seven-step ladder, and shipping it is the last step
rules.divergesFromPhp: PHP's own minors have broken running applications, and a Composer library forwards its dependencies' breaks as its own; here a dependency-forced break reaches a program author only after adapting, wrapping, compensating, holding, vendoring and replacing have all been tried

rules.title: A forced user-facing break survives one minor release as a warning naming its replacement, and is removed in the next major
rules.divergesFromPhp: PHP's deprecation notices are runtime `E_DEPRECATED` output a production `error_reporting` hides; here the warning is the compiler's, and a warning that does not name the replacement is not a deprecation

rules.title: A dependency move never fixes a guard test by editing its threshold, and it regenerates the attribution file in the same commit
Each dependency bump is its own commit, classified in its message
Being current has a schedule, a stale dependency is a defect, and a human fires every pass — never an agent, cron or CI
rules.divergesFromPhp: a PHP shop's `composer update` and the runtime's own upgrade are separate projects on nobody's calendar; here the toolchain, every crate, CI actions and the PHP oracle move on one dated cadence

rules.title: A third-party extension is a sandboxed WebAssembly component, never a shared library loaded with `dlopen`
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `extension=` line and no `.so`; an extension is one portable `.nvsx` that cannot address host memory, and nothing loads native code at runtime

rules.title: Library and extension code sits at one of three tiers: built-in, sandboxed component, or statically linked native
A `.nvsx` is a single WebAssembly component whose manifest is an `nvs.manifest` custom section
rules.divergesFromPhp: a PHP extension is a per-platform binary registered by an ini line; an `.nvsx` is one file for every platform and carries its own declarations inside it

rules.title: An extension package may carry Novis source beside its `.nvsx`, under one namespace, and the component's manifest registers exactly one class
rules.divergesFromPhp: a Composer package is source only and a PHP extension is a binary only; an extension package here is both, and the builder a program names is ordinary Novis source

rules.title: An extension loads only from an `[[extension]]` entry in the root-owned `nvs.toml`, pinned by its `sha256`
rules.divergesFromPhp: `extension=` in a `php.ini` names a file; an `[[extension]]` entry names a file and its digest, a project cannot add one, and a changed binary under its pin is refused rather than loaded

rules.title: An extension's classes are registered from its manifest at load, and a call into one is type-checked at compile time and emitted as a direct call
rules.divergesFromPhp: a call into an extension is checked by `nvs check` like a call into `Core`, not dispatched by name at runtime

rules.title: A value crosses the guest boundary as a bounds-checked handle, never as a pointer
A guest is instantiated fresh for each request that calls it, so extension state cannot leak between requests
rules.divergesFromPhp: a stateful PHP extension keeps its globals for the worker's lifetime; a guest starts pristine on every request and nothing it stored is there on the next one

rules.title: A guest runs under the request's CPU and memory caps, and a runaway guest traps rather than hanging a core
A guest has no ambient authority: WASI is not granted by default, and every host function it receives is capability-checked
rules.divergesFromPhp: native extension code calls `open()` and `connect()` directly; a guest reaches the filesystem and the network only through the same grants script code has

rules.title: An extension call costs a fixed ten-odd nanoseconds over a built-in call, so an extension's API is coarse-grained
A C dependency is admitted under ordinary audit only if attacker-controlled data never reaches it; otherwise it needs an exceptional verification record or is confined to wasm
PDF is a decode-only format of `nvs/image`, in the second wave, and never a member of `nvs/pdf`
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no Ghostscript to install and no ImageMagick policy to loosen; a page becomes an image through the same sandboxed component every other format uses

rules.title: `nvs service` is a namespace, and everything after a mandatory `--` is stored verbatim as the argv the service runs
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no shim — no NSSM, no WinSW, no hand-written unit around `php-fpm` — and the hosted program's own flags follow a `--` the installer never reads past

rules.title: The service installer fails closed: a closed `serve`/`run` allowlist, no relative path, no argv without `--config`, no install whose output goes nowhere, no password on a command line
rules.divergesFromPhp: `sc create` and a hand-written unit store whatever they are given; the installer refuses each of these by name with an `E063x` diagnostic and installs nothing

rules.title: On Windows the argv is encoded into the SCM's one `ImagePath` string, the binary path is always quoted, and nothing else holds it
A service's default identity is the local system account, and `--account` names any other, the per-service virtual account included
rules.divergesFromPhp: a hand-registered service runs as `LocalSystem`, and so does one installed here with no `--account`; the per-service virtual account and its grants are one `--account` away

rules.title: A stop drains, a `PARAMCHANGE` reloads, and lifecycle records go to the event log beside the configured log destination
rules.divergesFromPhp: a shim can only report that the process exited; the service itself reports an advancing stop checkpoint and performs a reload in-process

rules.title: On Linux `nvs service unit` prints the systemd unit and touches nothing; writing it is an explicit `--install`
rules.divergesFromPhp: the unit is generated rather than written by hand, and printing rather than installing is the default because configuration management owns the directory

rules.title: The generated unit carries the hardening block, `Type=notify`, `MemoryMax` from `[limits]`, and `AmbientCapabilities` only for a privileged port
rules.divergesFromPhp: `NoNewPrivileges`, `ProtectSystem=strict` and an emptied `CapabilityBoundingSet` are emitted for you rather than left to whoever writes the unit

rules.title: A single-file bundle may not install itself as a service
There is no `Core\Service`: only an operator installs a service, from the command line, and nothing about it is on the request path
